lead.question: The smallest unresolved absolutely maximally entangled states
lead.title: The smallest unresolved absolutely maximally entangled states

review.statement: For each pair (n,d) ∈ {(8,4),(7,6)}, set k = ⌊n/2⌋. Does there exist a unit vector ψ ∈ (ℂᵈ)⊗ⁿ such that, for every k-party subset S, Tr_{Sᶜ}(|ψ⟩⟨ψ|) = I_{dᵏ}/dᵏ? The catalogue asks for a decision on either pair and treats the two cases separately. [Pinned catalogue entry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgmcm/problems/6eea3514ab25dc2c3f19bc7bebbd80aef7066ce4/catalogue/problems/034_smallest_open_ame_cases.txt)
review.significance: AME(7,6) exists. On 2 August 2026, after the catalogue’s 20 July status check, Shi, Zhang, Zhao and Li gave an explicit construction. Setting q = 3 in their Eq. (40) gives local dimension 2q = 6. Their Theorem 1 establishes existence for every integer local dimension d ≥ 3 at seven parties. AME(8,4) remains open in the literature located through 26 November 2026, including Pandya’s November update. [Seven-party construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.01011) · [November status discussion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17216)
review.settlement_test: A positive resolution requires one exact normalized state and a proof covering all required reductions: all 35 triples equal I₂₁₆/216 for AME(7,6), or all 70 four-party reductions equal I₂₅₆/256 for AME(8,4). A negative resolution requires proving that every normalized complex state fails at least one reduction. The cited construction meets the positive criterion for AME(7,6), which suffices for the catalogue’s either-case request.
review.aliases: AME(8,4) is an eight-party 4-uniform pure state of local dimension four, also called an eight-leg perfect tensor of bond dimension four. AME(7,6) is a seven-party 3-uniform pure state of local dimension six. Both are instances of Open Quantum Problem 35, “Existence of absolutely maximally entangled pure states.”
